title: The Global Debt Crisis JUST Got Twice as Bad.
speaker: Kevin Paffrath

macro_themes.view: JPMorgan analysis shows shadow default rate ~16% (doubling) in $1.3T private credit; more worrying than AI debt because zombie bankruptcies cause permanent layoffs.
AI bond weakness (e.g. CoreWeave) reflects heavy new issuance, not necessarily rising default risk; GPU collateral retains value.
Personally holds no debt; fine buying great companies and housing with little/no debt despite bubble fears.
Deals like the Bumble buyout show the cycle is still in its 'early drunk days'.

calls.reason: 10-year at 24-year highs; may have just peaked giving some breathing room, but the uptrend is obvious and adds stress to indebted borrowers.
calls.quote: It seems like it recently peaked, which a little bit of uh, know, a breather. ... but this, the trend here is pretty obvious.

calls.reason: Stock down from $187 to ~$77; bonds trade at junk (~15% yield) as heavy new AI issuance competes for money; ~$10B cash vs ~$18B bills. But GPU collateral keeps residual value, so not a sign the AI market is collapsing. No explicit stock bias.
calls.quote: I agree there is excess. I agree CoreWeave doesn't have money.

notes: Solo commentary video (not an interview); classified as macro_interview as closest type. Recording time not stated. Bumble take-private at $6.08 discussed critically but no trading call.
